newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open stronger on CPI data, dlr gains.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open stronger on CPI data, dlr gains.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened stronger on Tuesday, rallying amid a lower-than-expected rise in the U.S. consumer price index and a sharp rise in the value of the Canadian dollar, analysts said.
"The CPI data was what really got things going," said Mark Chandler, a senior economist with Goldman Sachs Canada in Toronto. "Canada is also getting a boost from the Canadian dollar."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.70 to C$107.70 to yield 7.333 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond rose 28/32 to yield 7.10 percent.
The spread between the two bonds widened to 23 basis points from 22 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.

Canadian bonds strengthened after the U.S. March consumer price index allayed market fears of an acceleration in price growth, sparking a rally in U.S. debt markets and easing the pressure on Federal Reserve policymakers to raise interest rates there.

Speculation that the U.S. Federal Reserve will be less willing to raise rates in turn sparked a rally in the Canadian dollar, which strenthened to C$1.3939 (US$0.7174) from its open at C$1.3982 (US$0.7152).
While the U.S. data did not dispel expectations that the Fed will hike rates in May, "there's a feeling that inflation may not be that bad," said Goldman's Chandler.
In other prices, the Canadian 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.60 to C$101.40 to yield 6.798 percent while the U.S. bond rose 21/32 to yield 6.88 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to eight basis points from 10 basis points on Monday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.16 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.29 percent.
